name: Stomach vacuum / waist training

lead: The stomach vacuum is an exercise in which the abdomen is drawn inward, aimed at the transversus abdominis, the deepest of the four front abdominal wall muscles. Users practice it for a tighter abdominal wall and a smaller-looking waist that supports a V-taper.

The muscle is well described anatomically, but evidence on this use is thin: a looksmax.org thread has a user reporting he nearly lost the ability to do it and regained it with renewed training. Wikipedia notes it is disputed whether training this deep core muscle specifically is worthwhile, and a 2011 study found abdominal exercise alone does not reduce abdominal fat or girth.

paras: People practice it as a hold, drawing the belly in toward the spine, usually fitted into a warm-up or daily routine alongside regular training and fat loss. Waist training is sometimes also used for compression garments, which this entry does not cover.
No harms data were found for the exercise itself.

angle.text: Users practice the stomach vacuum to train the transversus abdominis and make the waist look smaller, supporting a V-taper. The muscle is well described anatomically. Research on this use is thin, and abdominal exercise alone does not reduce belly fat or girth according to a 2011 study.

lead: The stomach vacuum is an abdominal exercise in which the belly button is drawn inward toward the spine by contracting the deep abdominal muscles, mainly the transversus abdominis, with little use of the diaphragm.[1] People practice it for a flatter, tighter-looking midsection and a smaller apparent waist; Wikipedia says it is used for a leaner midsection in bodybuilding competitions.[1]

The transversus abdominis is the deepest of the flat abdominal muscles and is often called the corset muscle because pulling the abdomen inward creates girdle-like tension around the midsection.[2] Looksmaxxing discussion treats training it as a way to improve waist appearance without compression garments.

Community material is limited to short forum posts, such as a looksmax.org thread in which a user says he nearly lost the ability to perform it two years earlier and can do it easily again after resuming training.[3] No clinical studies were found.

paras: Wikipedia describes the vacuum exercise as contracting the internal abdominal muscles, with repetitions that can serve as light aerobic or light strength work.[1] Strength can be built, it says, by drawing the muscle in further, contracting harder or holding longer, and some people use a string tied at navel level as feedback.[1] Wikipedia also notes disputed benefit and healthiness of doing it while lifting.[1]

The abdominal exercise article describes the transversus abdominis as part of the four-muscle abdominal wall and says focused training of this deep core muscle is disputed, with some experts recommending broader regimens.[4]

The phrase waist training is also used for wearing compression garments such as corsets; this entry concerns the muscle exercise. Related practices include hypopressive exercises, which Wikipedia says are thought to raise abdominal wall and pelvic floor tone and reduce resting waist circumference.[1]

The abdominal exercise article states that whether abdominal exercise reduces belly fat is highly disputed, citing a 2011 study that found abdominal exercises alone were not enough to reduce abdominal fat and girth, and adds that fat reduction requires an energy deficit.[4] Wikipedia notes that the effectiveness of transversus abdominis training is debated, with some reviews finding its function does not reliably predict low back pain outcomes.[2]

lore.intro: Discussion on looksmax.org is brief and anecdotal [3].

claims.claim: The stomach vacuum skill can be lost and regained with training.
